messages:
Sam B: Hey team — customer reports intermittent streaming cutouts when requests route through their corporate proxy. Two request IDs from traces: req_01FX9K2J4 and req_01FY2L8B1 (both ~2026-11-02T14:12:xxZ). I have full traces but need a minimal HTTP replay/cURL snippet to validate whether the proxy or our token rotation is the root cause. Any quick repro/playbook?

infra-bot: Deploy job rtx-service/2026-11-02 finished at 14:10 UTC (no rollbacks triggered).

Devon L: Is the stream using SSE (text/event-stream) or chunked JSON? Also are clients on http/1.1 or http/2? Proxy behavior differs a lot by protocol.

Sam B: Chunked JSON (application/json; charset=utf-8). Clients use http/1.1. Proxy is corporate gateway that sometimes injects/changes Connection and may mutate keep-alive pooling. From one trace, headers we saw:```
GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
X-Request-ID: req_01FX9K2J4
User-Agent: AcmeSDK/2.1
Connection: keep-alive
Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate
```

Maria G: For chunked JSON streaming the usual minimal cURL I use is:```
curl -v -N --http1.1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_local_replay_$(date +%s)" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=small" \
  -d '{"input":"smoke test","stream":true}'```
Notes: -N disables buffering in curl so chunks arrive to stdout; --http1.1 forces h1 behavior; use --trace-ascii ./trace.txt to capture raw bytes for attach. Also include --no-buffer (on some builds) or pipe through stdbuf -o0 if needed.

Sam B: Helpful. Customer says proxy sometimes rotates a signed cookie (HMAC) and then the stream gets cut with a 401 mid-stream. How can I simulate a short-lived cookie or HMAC rotation in the replay?

Maria G: You can simulate by injecting a Cookie header and toggling its value between requests. Example:```
curl -v -N --http1.1 \
  -H "Cookie: signed_session=payload_OLD|deadbeefhmac" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_sim_12345" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=small" \
  -d '{"input":"test","stream":true}'```
To emulate rotation mid-stream run one curl with an old cookie then immediately open a second connection with a new cookie/value to see if the proxy connection pool hands traffic to a backend with different auth state. Another trick: set a custom timestamp header the proxy validates, e.g. -H "X-Client-Ts: 2026-11-02T14:12:00Z" and increment it to simulate skew.

Alex P: Also try toggling Connection header to force socket teardown on proxy: Connection: close vs keep-alive. If Connection: close prevents the cutouts it points to keep-alive pooling reuse. Capture packet-level evidence with tcpdump on the client side or ask customer to capture proxy logs showing connection reuse (pool id, backend selection).

Devon L: Minimal checklist for Sam to run and attach: 1) Run the Maria curl with --trace-ascii and attach trace.txt. 2) Rerun with Cookie set to an expired HMAC and attach logs. 3) Try Connection: close. 4) If still flaky, capture the first 30s of tcpdump or netcat capture. Please paste the curl --trace output here (redact tokens). :thumbsup:

Sam B: I'll run the three variants and post the trace outputs (redacting Authorization). Thanks — will update in ~30m.

Maria G: Thanks — if you get a reproducible trace, we can craft a short test that our infra team can run from the same region to validate proxy config changes.

Sam B: Uploaded trace snippets to the ticket. Follow-ups incoming.
